NoteTexAccessor::wrap_inline_math¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::wrap_inline_math(std::string_view delim) const

Wrap Each Cell As Inline Math, Unless It Already Looks Like Math¶

wrap_inline_math() trims each cell and wraps it as inline TeX math: delim + content + delim. An empty delim defaults to $; any non-empty delim is used verbatim as both the leading and trailing delimiter — there is no asymmetric open/close pairing, so wrap_inline_math("~") on a=b produces ~a=b~, not a matched pair of distinct characters.

This method skips a cell that already contains a math marker. If the trimmed cell contains a $, \(, or \[ anywhere in it, the cell is returned completely unchanged — no delimiter is added, and the check does not require the existing marker to be balanced or even at the edges of the cell. Contrast this with wrap_display_math, which has no such check and always wraps a non-empty cell, nesting any existing delimiters one level inside the new ones. A cell that is empty after trimming is returned empty either way, with no delimiter added.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Undefined input remains undefined; Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes receivers are rejected because TeX source is Text.

Example 1: Default Delimiter, Empty Cell, And Two Kinds Of Existing Math¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"x+y", "", "$already$", R"(\(also\))"})
              .tex().wrap_inline_math("")
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["$x+y$", "", "$already$", "\\(also\\)"]

The first cell, with no existing math marker, gets $...$. The empty second cell stays empty. The third and fourth cells already contain a $ and a \( respectively, so both are returned completely unmodified — not even a check for whether the marker is balanced.

Example 2: Idempotent By Construction¶

const auto wrapped = pluss::make_note({"x+y"}).tex().wrap_inline_math("");
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << (wrapped.tex().wrap_inline_math("") == wrapped).all().bool_item()
          << '\n';

Output¶

true

Once a cell has been wrapped, it contains $, so a second call’s existing-marker check leaves it unchanged.

Example 3: A Custom Delimiter Is Used On Both Sides¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"a=b"}).tex().wrap_inline_math("~") << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["~a=b~"]

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().wrap_inline_math("").defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().wrap_inline_math("");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "wrap inline math Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
wrap inline math Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • wrap_display_math: the display counterpart, which always wraps regardless of existing delimiters.

  • add_math_delimiters: choose inline or display wrapping automatically per cell instead of committing to one form.

  • math_only: extract existing math content rather than adding new delimiters.
